newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks at 3rd record in week on jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks at 3rd record in week on jobs data.

text.p: Mexican stocks continued their heady journey into uncharted territory Friday, chalking up their third record close of the week.
Traders said confirmation of optimistic forecasts for unemployment data buttressed midday gains.
"The market was firm, buyers stepped in after the unemployment data were released," a desk trader said.
Final closing figures put the blue-chip IPC index at a record 3,880.04 points, a gain of 40.31 points, or 1.05 percent.
Mexican open unemployment in January was 4.5 percent, compared to 6.4 percent for the same month in 1996, the National Statistics Institute announced in late trading.
A Reuters survey of financial professionals in Mexico showed they had forecast an average rate of 4.84 percent.
Falling unemployment is not generally seen as a sign of an overheating economy in Mexico, and does not therefore fuel pressure on interest rates and weaken the currency.
Other traders said a turnaround by the Dow Jones industrial average, albeit moderate, persuaded buyers to get off the fence and enter the market after slow early trade.
The Dow ended up 4.24 points, or 0.06 percent, at 6,931.62 points.

American Depository Receipts -- shares in foreign companies traded in the United States -- listed by market heavyweight Telmex ended up 1/8 at 40, while their L shares gained 4 centavos (one cent) to 15.56 pesos ($2.01). The stock accounted for 13 percent of all shares traded during the session.
On the broad market, 113 stocks changed hands. Advancers beat decliners 69 to 25.
Construction firm Tribasa led the gainers' list on news its Chilean subsidiary will issue bonds to cover a loan contracted to build a toll road, traders said.
Tribasa nominal shares rose 2.45 pesos (32 cents) to close at 27.30 pesos ($3.52).

Retail chain Comerci UBC and UB stocks topped the decliners' list in the wake of news the company would buy a Mexican operation jointly held by Kmart and another Mexican retail chain, El Puerto de Liverpool.
Traders were divided on the reasons for the slump, which came after sharp gains Thursday ahead of the announcement.
Some traders said it was "selling on the news after buying on the rumour."
Other traders expressed doubts over Comerci's capacity to pay for the acquisition.
Comerci UBC units ended off 56 centavos (7 cents) at 6.90 pesos (89 cents), while the UBC series fell 54 centavos to 7.00 pesos (90 cents).
